title: The CEO Who Bought a Town, Then Made Residents Pay for Air
hook: One company patented the air in an entire town and charged residents to breathe.
why_this_can_go_viral: The absurdity of patenting air triggers disbelief and outrage, driving shares and comments.

title: The Trader Who Used a Fake Earthquake to Crash an Entire Industry
hook: A single fake seismic report wiped out $3 billion in market value before lunch.
why_this_can_go_viral: The scale and audacity of using a natural disaster lie shocks viewers, making them want to understand how.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Mind Reading' Tech—It Was Just a Mic in Your Wall
hook: Investors poured millions into a 'neural decoder' that was actually just recording conversations through drywall.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blends tech hype with creepy surveillance, creating a 'can't believe they got away with it' reaction.

title: The Company That Bought Every Graveyard—Then Charged Families Rent for Graves
hook: A single corporation now owns 1 in 3 cemeteries and bills families annually for 'grave maintenance subscriptions'.
why_this_can_go_viral: Profiting from death in such a direct way triggers universal moral outrage and fear.

title: The Chemist Who Discovered His 'Safe' Food Dye Was Slowly Paralyzing Children
hook: He found the proof in his own lab, but his bosses burned the study and sold the dye for 14 more years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines a relatable fear (processed food) with a heroic whistleblower arc and a horrific health outcome.

title: The Ad Company That Used Your Phone's Gyroscope to Guess Your Mood and Sell to It
hook: They didn't track what you typed—they tracked how you walked, and knew you were sad before you did.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that your phone knows your emotions is deeply unsettling, highly shareable, and sparks privacy debates.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Fresh' Orange Juice—Made From Oranges Picked 18 Months Ago
hook: They kept the juice in giant chemical vats, de-oxygenated, then added 'fresh' flavor packets at bottling.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals a disgusting truth about a daily staple; viewers will share to warn friends.

title: The Doctor Who Discovered His Hospital Was Reusing Single-Use Heart Catheters
hook: He found bloody packaging in a dumpster—the hospital was washing, repackaging, and reselling 'sterile' devices.
why_this_can_go_viral: Directly threatens viewers' sense of safety in hospitals; visceral disgust and anger drive shares.

title: The Trader Who Made $100 Million Off a Fake Alien Invasion Broadcast
hook: He rented a pirate radio station, broadcast a 'breaking news' alert, and shorted defense stocks before the correction.
why_this_can_go_viral: The outlandish premise (aliens + insider trading) is incredibly clickable and sounds like fiction.

title: The CEO Who Made Employees Wear 'Happiness' Helmets That Shocked Them When They Frowned
hook: He called it 'productivity optimization'—the electrodes delivered a 20-volt jolt every time a smile dropped.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shock value is extreme; viewers will be horrified and share the unbelievable violation of human rights.

title: The Sugar Company That Paid Scientists to Say 'Fat Is the Enemy' for 50 Years
hook: They funded a Harvard study that blamed butter, not sugar, for heart disease—and changed global diet forever.
why_this_can_go_viral: A massive, decades-long conspiracy that changed everyone's health; 'I knew it!' factor drives engagement.

title: The Startup That Sold 'AI Hiring'—It Was Just a Random Name Picker
hook: The algorithm was a roulette wheel coded in Excel, and it still got a $50 million valuation.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes the emperor's-new-clothes nature of AI hype; 'I knew it was fake!' validation.

title: The Landlord Who Bought Every Street Light—Then Charged Pedestrians to Walk at Night
hook: He privatized the lampposts, turned off the lights unless you paid a monthly 'safety subscription', and sued a jogger.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd real-world feudalism that anyone can imagine happening in their own city.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Fighter Jet Blueprint by Analyzing the Compressor Blade Dust
hook: He didn't steal plans—he swept the factory floor, analyzed the metal shavings, and reverse-engineered the engine.
why_this_can_go_viral: Sounds like a mission from a spy thriller; the cleverness of the method is highly shareable.

title: The Supplier That Sold 'Cotton' Shirts—Made From Ground-Up Plastic Bottles From Hospitals
hook: The 'recycled fabric' came from biohazard bins: IV bags, syringes, and surgical gloves melted into threads.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visceral disgust + environmental hypocrisy creates a powerful emotional reaction.

title: The Oil Company That Dumped Toxic Sludge Into a Dead Volcano—Then Called It 'Geothermal Storage'
hook: They pumped millions of gallons of chemical waste into a dormant volcano and claimed it was 'carbon capture'.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines environmental rage with a spectacularly dangerous method; 'they put WHAT in a volcano?'.

title: The Founder Who Sold His 'Cancer Cure' Startup—It Was Just Bleach and Baking Soda
hook: He convinced billionaires his 'pH therapy' cured tumors, and when patients died, he blamed their 'negative energy'.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits hope and fear; the cruelty of faking a cure is universally rage-inducing.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Water Well in a Desert—Then Sold Water Back at 1000x Price
hook: A single corporation now owns the only three aquifers in a 200-mile radius and charges a village's GDP per gallon.
why_this_can_go_viral: Water is life; privatizing it feels like the ultimate evil, sparking outrage and debate.

title: The Trader Who Used a Fake Celebrity Death to Pump and Dump a Penny Stock
hook: He tweeted that a rapper died, bought the stock at the dip, then sold when the 'memorial frenzy' hit peak.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable platform (Twitter) + morbid scam; viewers love seeing how easy market manipulation is.

title: The Clothing Brand That Used 'Sweatshop Free' Labels—While Paying Workers in Scrip That Lost Value Daily
hook: Workers were paid in company-store credits that hyperinflated every month, trapping them in eternal debt.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes the dark truth behind 'ethical' labels; moral outrage drives sharing.

title: The Chemist Who Saw His Company Sell 'Organic' Apples—Grown in Soil Laced with Chemical Fertilizer
hook: The 'organic' farm was certified, but the soil was still saturated with banned pesticides from a previous owner.
why_this_can_go_viral: People pay a premium for organic; discovering it's fake is a direct personal betrayal.

title: The CEO Who Bribed a Government Official with a 'Lifetime Achievement' Award—Then a Cushion Job
hook: He created a fake non-profit, gave the official a $500,000 'award', and hired him as a 'consultant' the next day.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes how easily the system is gamed; 'they didn't even try to hide it' outrage.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Luxury Watch Company's Movement by Attending Their Baselworld Party
hook: He didn't case the vault—he drugged the CEO's champagne, photographed the prototype, and replaced it before morning.
why_this_can_go_viral: High-stakes heist story with a luxury angle; sounds like a James Bond scene.
